main_diagnosis: The simulator shows very poor likelihood (high neg-log-marginal) most likely because of two implementation defects: (1) several parameter signs are inverted at extraction (E_leak, Vt, param_i, param_j), which will systematically flip thresholds and reversal potentials and break all gating kinetics; and (2) the two pre-allocated extra channels (gbar_X1 / gbar_X2) are read from params but never used in kinetics, membrane conductance, or state updates. Fixing the sign errors and implementing (at most) one additional, slow potassium-type channel (to provide spike-frequency regulation without introducing bursting) should substantially reduce the discrepancy with experimental tonic-spiking data while keeping the model parsimonious.

issues.description: Parameter sign inversions during extraction: E_leak, Vt, param_i and param_j are negated when read from params (lines where params[:,3], params[:,4], params[:,8], params[:,9] are assigned). These negative assignments flip biologically meaningful signs (reversal potentials and voltage offsets / time constants), corrupting gating functions and all downstream dynamics.
issues.location: forward() parameter extraction (gbar_Na..param_j assignments near top of forward)
issues.suggestion: Remove the explicit negations so that parameters are used with their intended sign (e.g., E_leak = params[:,3].float(), Vt = params[:,4].float(), param_i = params[:,8].float(), param_j = params[:,9].float()). Add input validation / asserts on ranges (e.g., reasonable bounds for E_leak, Vt, time-constant scale) and unit-tests that check simple behaviors (e.g., resting potential with zero injection equals leak reversal). This will restore correct voltage dependence of alpha/beta rates and prevent systematic bias in fitted parameters.

issues.description: Unused extra channel slots (X1/X2): gbar_X1 and gbar_X2 are parsed but never contribute to tau_V_inv, V_inf, or state updates; no gating variables or kinetics are implemented for them. As a result the model cannot capture missing currents that the data requires (e.g., a slow, non-bursting K-type adaptation current) and must compensate by mis-fitting other parameters.
issues.location: forward() editable sections (kinetics, tau_V_inv, V_inf, state vars, and state updates)
issues.suggestion:
Implement at most one parsimonious extra channel (use X1) to capture slow spike-frequency regulation without introducing bursting. Recommended implementation: a non-inactivating, voltage-dependent K current (M-type) with one activation gating variable p. Use gbar_X1 as conductance, use param_i as half-activation voltage V_half (mV) and param_j as a baseline time constant tau_base (ms). Example recipe to add in the editable blocks:
- p_inf(V) = 1.0 / (1 + exp((V - V_half)/k)) with k≈5–10 mV (fix k=6 or make small constant)
- tau_p(V) = tau_base + tau_scaling/(1 + exp((V - V_half)/k_tau)) (or a simple constant tau_p = tau_base)
- Include the channel in tau_V_inv: + gbar_X1 * p[:,i-1]
- Include in V_inf numerator: + gbar_X1 * p[:,i-1] * E_K (use E_K or a separate reversal if desired)
- Initialize p[:,0]=p_inf(V[:,0]) and update p in the loop similar to n/m/h using tau_x/inf_x or directly with p_inf and tau_p.
This keeps model complexity low (only one extra gating variable and two tunable params) and produces slow outward current that reduces spike count and shapes mean/variance without producing bursts. After implementing, re-run fitting and check the seven summary statistics; if improvement stalls, try small adjustments (e.g., tune k or use X2 for a persistent Na if strictly necessary).
